proof.criterion: Each changed loop is driven by the change it serves and does nothing while nothing changes; every periodic statement left at idle is named
proof.surface: Two real head processes on one database and NATS beside two fork-point processes, every loop on (fake Azure embedder, fake GitHub App), statements counted by source from the Postgres statement log over a 10-minute idle window
proof.observed: Both processes, 10 minutes: 5,402 statements before, 4,011 after (4.50 -> 3.34 per second per process); CPU 0.0035/0.0032 -> 0.0029/0.0031 cores. Embedding scan 240 -> 0, coverage 34 -> 0, task progress 8 -> 0, reference excerpts 12 -> 0, suggestion outcomes 70 -> 0, edit notices 481 -> 0, delivery settings reads 42 -> 3; shared listener keep-alive 0 -> 40. The remaining timers (heartbeat 5 s, outbox 5 s, block index 30 s, standby durable reconcile 30 s, settlement 1 min, keep-alives 30 s, redelivery 2 min, reconcile and import 5 min) are named with why no event replaces each in the PR body.

proof.criterion: Edit notices are sent when a notice falls due, not on a five-second sweep
proof.surface: The head binary's HTTP API: a session writes a spec, a person writes a new version through POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits
proof.observed: The person's edit opened a notice due 30 s later (18:39:11.959); the sweep ran once on the write's notify (nothing due), made no edit-notice statement from 18:38:42.036 to 18:39:11.969, then sent the notice 10 ms after due: 'dispatch: sent edit notices notices=1', row deleted, artifact.human_edited delivered on the spec author's agent topic.
proof.negativeControl: With no notice due, no statement mentioning edit-notices or document_edit_notices in 125 s.

proof.criterion: The timers the plan keeps are jittered every period (the webhook redelivery sweep included)
proof.surface: The two head processes' and two fork-point processes' webhook-redelivery lease attempts in their Dispatch logs and the statement log
proof.observed: Head: the two processes' attempts fell 4.6, 0.8, 2.8, 10.7, 5.8, 2.1 and 0.6 s apart; one process's periods were 124.3, 129.8, 123.3, 129.0, 126.3 and 124.2 s. The test passes: a sweep at start, then gaps in [interval, 1.1 x interval).
proof.negativeControl: Fork point (plain ticker): both processes tried at exactly 120 s intervals, 24-41 ms apart, every period.

proof.criterion: The GitHub intake handles pull requests concurrently and in order across a hand-over; its stop fits the stop grace; a failed subscribe leaves nothing a reconnect binds; write-woken loops catch up after a listener outage
proof.surface: The real binary at c83c0851 in config B (same intake, listener and loop code as the head; the head adds the edit-notice wake and the redelivery jitter)
proof.observed: Comment embedded 288 ms after its POST; listener backend terminated, redial in 1.16 s, outage comment embedded 48 ms after the new LISTEN; GitHub holding a fetch 50 s: exit 15.06 s after SIGTERM with the hand-back line; three fetches of one pull request across a hand-over with no overlap; NATS down while subscribing: bound once on its own bind poll, no resubscribe, the pull request fetched once and acknowledged; 1x before 47/244/574 ms, after 48/254/843 ms.
proof.negativeControl: GitHub answering at once: exit 0.07 s after SIGTERM with no hand-back line; the fork point re-bound the failed subscription on reconnect ('envoy nats resubscribing').
